camera.setups: Virtual 2D camera per shot: zoom 1.0 to 1.1 push-ins, punch-ins to 1.75, pull-outs from 1.6, sine handheld drift 3-4 px, parallax layers in the day scenes (sky 0.08, clouds 0.14, cliffs 0.3, sea 0.45, deck 1.0)
camera.gear_guess: HTML canvas rendered frame by frame (code)

lighting.lighting_overall: Flat cartoon light: one hard cel band on the right of each shape, contact shadows; light sources are additive radial glows (sun, lantern, light shaft) and full-frame tints (heat, darkness, flash)

grade.grade_overall: Bright saturated day world (cool sky over warm wood), then near-black and navy for the dark part, warm lantern amber at the end; every frame has a soft violet vignette and light film grain

editing.editing: About 12 setups for 10 lines (2 to 5 s each, the mechanism longest); whip pans (0.2 s out + 0.2 s in, 420 px horizontal slide with heavy motion blur) between places, hard cuts inside a sequence and into black; every shot has its own camera: slow push-in plus handheld drift, punch-ins on reveals; impacts are a burst, a 0.25 s shake and a warm flash

format.format: Vertical 9:16 code-animated stick-figure 'what if / why' explainer, 37 s, narrated (TTS male, about 3 words/s) over a plucked underscore with many cartoon sound effects; 1-2 word lowercase captions

style.render_style: Code-drawn 2D vector cartoon on canvas: flat saturated fills, ink outlines, one hard cel shadow band, additive glows; stick people with big round white heads in a detailed bright world
style.outline: One dark warm violet-grey ink (L about 0.24) on everything: about 5 px on props and scenery, 12 px on the big diagram, 1.7% of figure height on characters; limbs are round-capped strokes 2.8% of height; clouds outlined in pale blue instead
style.shading: Flat base, one hard-edged darker band (dark violet at 16 to 18%) over the right 30 to 40% of each shape, a thin pale strip on the left; soft dark ellipse contact shadows at 22%; light as additive radial glows and full-frame tints
style.shape_language: Round and soft: bean torsos, circle heads (radius 0.19 of the figure height), stick limbs with dot hands and oval feet; props as rounded rectangles and bulging curves; tall wobbly pillars with blob tops; perspective floors from a vanishing point above the frame
style.texture: Almost none: strata, plank and board lines as strokes; 7% overlay grain and a violet vignette over every frame
style.type_ui: Captions: 1-2 lowercase words, bold rounded sans, white with a dark outline and soft shadow, centred about 70% down, popping in with overshoot. In-scene words are rare and big: a yellow number with a thick ink stroke beside a clock icon, a red impact word in a yellow burst, a cream paper card with a serif title and a ticked checklist, a red rubber-stamp verdict
style.motion_style: Never still: per-shot push-ins and handheld drift, punch-ins on reveals, whip pans between places; keyframed acting with backOut overshoot, squash on landing, IK reaches to the face; impacts as burst + shake + flash; darkness reveals as a growing circular mask
style.signature: Stick people with big white heads and expressive brows and eyes in a bright saturated cartoon world; the dark beat as a near-black frame where only white eyes show; one big diagram on a full-frame radial glow with a number counting up beside a clock; a rubber-stamp verdict on a paper checklist; 1-2 word lowercase captions
style.do_not_copy: The topic and all its objects and places (pirates, eye patches, ships, the deck, cannons, barrels, crates with words, treasure chest, frying pans, the eye diagram), its script lines, the named TV show and its number; there is no watermark or handle

story.summary: A 'what if' question about a familiar object, then 'picture this' drops the viewer into the scene as a stick person; the others flee into darkness, the viewer follows and is blind and gets hit; the mechanism (how long the body needs to adapt, with one real number) is shown on a big diagram; the character who has been doing the odd thing all along uses it as the trick and can see; a real test is stamped plausible; the last line flips the hook.
story.hook: A close-up of the character with the familiar object, who lifts it to show the assumption is wrong, under a 'What if [familiar thing] had nothing to do with [assumed reason]?' line.
highlights: The viewer is a character ('you') living the problem, not a spectator
Slapstick consequences make the problem felt before it is explained
One clean diagram shot with a real number counting up
A proof beat (a real test) as a stamped checklist
The payoff sentence answers the hook by flipping it
